chunks: Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “ʿAmmār greeted the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم while he was in salat (prayer), and he responded to him.”
Then Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “Indeed, al-Salām is one of the names of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.أَسْمَاءِ اللَّهِ: the names of Allah, indicating divine attribution and sanctity
key_terms.السَّلَامُ: the greeting of peace; also a divine name of Allah in this context
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship being performed
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.عَمَّارٌ: ʿAmmār, the person who offered the greeting

ai.seo_question: Can a person in salat (prayer) return someone’s greeting of salām?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that returning a greeting during salat (prayer) was done by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also highlights the sanctity of the greeting of salām by stating that al-Salām is one of the names of Allah عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1066 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"Ammar greeted the Messenger of Allah (sw) while he was in prayer, and he responded to him."
Then Abu Ja'far (as) said: "Indeed, Salam (greeting) is one of the names of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."
